name: ejabberd
why: An Erlang XMPP server is a real door into a chat protocol and an unusual runtime, though it is a server product.

brief.what_it_is: ejabberd is an open-source realtime messaging server written in Erlang/OTP by ProcessOne. The README describes it as an XMPP server, MQTT broker and SIP service in one package. It takes client connections (XMPP on port 5222, server-to-server on 5269, MQTT on 1883 in the homepage's sample config) and handles chat, pub/sub, presence, message archives and push, backed by storage such as SQL, Redis or LDAP. It is a server you install and run, not a chat client.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as messaging infrastructure for organisations that would rather run their own messaging than hand it to someone else, built on open standards and running on hardware they own.
brief.how_it_works: The server is built on Erlang/OTP and its 'let-it-crash' fault-tolerance model, with all-active clustering and consistent-hashing across nodes. Behaviour is configured in an ejabberd.yml file that lists listeners and modules (for example mod_mam for archives, mod_muc for group chat, mod_pubsub, mod_push). It is administered with the ejabberdctl CLI, a REST API and a live web admin.

brief.install_notes: Available as a Homebrew formula, plus source compile (COMPILE.md), ProcessOne installers, GitHub Releases, Docker images (ecs and ejabberd containers, x64 and arm64) and OS packages. Homebrew's own caveat: if you face nodedown problems, add your machine name to /private/etc/hosts after 'localhost'. Setup is a config file (ejabberd.yml) plus DNS and TLS certificates for a real deployment; the README does not give a step-by-step first-run walkthrough, which lives in the docs site.
brief.standout: One server speaks XMPP, MQTT and SIP (with STUN/TURN for WebRTC) against a shared auth and storage layer, which is unusual next to single-protocol chat servers. The Erlang runtime is the other hook: hot code upgrades and clustering are part of the design rather than add-ons.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage lists latest release 26.09 dated September 30, 2026, and claims 24 years of continuous releases since 2002. The GitHub README has active CI, coverage and translation badges. I did not see a last-commit date, so I cannot confirm commit recency beyond the release date.
brief.caveats: Much of the homepage is vendor marketing and I could not verify its numbers: the 2M+ concurrent sessions per node, WhatsApp/Nintendo/BBC as customers, and the 400+ XMPP extensions are claims made by ProcessOne. The Community edition is GPLv2; Business Edition (from EUR 16,000/year) and the Fluux managed service are commercial and gated behind paid features such as mobile push at scale and LTS releases. The homepage's 'Secure by default' list is also vendor-stated. Operating it well takes real protocol and Erlang-ops knowledge; it is a server product, not a weekend toy.
quotes: The messaging server that keeps real-time under your control.
ejabberd is an open-source, robust, scalable and extensible realtime platform built using Erlang/OTP
We write messaging infrastructure for people who get paged when it stops.
